chains.title: The alternate allele creates a GABPA-dependent TERT promoter site

links.claim: GABPA is the leading candidate because TERT promoter hotspot mutations are known to create ETS-family binding sites with reported GABP involvement; the alternate G>A allele is expected to bind GABPA more strongly, but no case-specific occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied.
The variant changes a cis-regulatory site in the TERT promoter.
GABPA binding at the altered promoter increases TERT transcription.
In glioblastoma cells, increased TERT transcription could support telomerase activity.
Increased telomerase activity could contribute to glioblastoma development or maintenance.

predictions: The alternate promoter allele shows greater GABPA occupancy than the reference allele.
A mutant-versus-reference TERT promoter reporter effect is reduced by GABPA depletion.
falsified_if: In an informative glioblastoma model, the alternate allele shows no increase in GABPA occupancy and the promoter effect is not reduced by GABPA depletion.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The alternate allele has no reproducible TF-dependent effect on TERT promoter activity in a relevant model.
Any association with disease could reflect another causal event, linkage, or a non-causal passenger mutation.
falsified_if: The alternate allele reproducibly increases TERT expression in a relevant model, with the effect dependent on binding of a specific TF.

chains.title: An alternate-allele ETS1 site increases TERT transcription

links.claim: ETS1 is a lower-priority ETS-family alternative to GABPA; the alternate allele is expected to strengthen its binding based on the created ETS-like motif, but no case-specific occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied.
The variant changes a cis-regulatory site in the TERT promoter.
ETS1 binding at the altered promoter increases TERT transcription.
In glioblastoma cells, increased TERT transcription could support telomerase activity.
Increased telomerase activity could contribute to glioblastoma development or maintenance.

predictions: The alternate promoter allele shows greater ETS1 occupancy than the reference allele.
A mutant-versus-reference TERT promoter reporter effect persists after GABPA depletion but is reduced by ETS1 depletion.
falsified_if: ETS1 depletion does not affect the mutant promoter effect, while GABPA depletion abolishes it.

matrix.test: Compare matched reference and mutant TERT promoter reporters in a glioblastoma line, with and without GABPA depletion.

outcomes.outcome: The mutant reporter has higher activity, and the increase is reduced by GABPA depletion.
The mutant reporter has higher activity, but the increase persists after GABPA depletion.
There is no reproducible mutant-versus-reference activity difference.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific GABPA occupancy at the endogenous TERT promoter in a mutation-positive glioblastoma model.

outcomes.outcome: GABPA occupancy is enriched on the alternate allele.
No specific alternate-allele GABPA enrichment is expected.
No reproducible alternate-allele GABPA enrichment is expected.

matrix.test: Compare matched reference and mutant TERT promoter reporters with and without ETS1 depletion.

outcomes.outcome: The mutant reporter effect is not specifically dependent on ETS1.
The mutant reporter has higher activity, and the increase is reduced by ETS1 depletion.
There is no reproducible mutant-versus-reference activity difference.

next_experiment: Run the matched reference-versus-mutant TERT promoter reporter in a glioblastoma line with and without GABPA depletion. It is the most direct proposed test of the leading GABPA chain against the null: a mutant-specific increase that depends on GABPA supports H1, whereas no reproducible allele effect supports H3.
